item.title: 1: Daily Halacha: Origins of Selihot During Elul
item.description:
Where does the custom of Selihot come from? It is not found in the Gemara or Midrash but is post-Talmudic, recorded by the Geonim of Babylonia in the ninth and tenth centuries, including Rav Kohen Sedek and Rav Hai Gaon, and mentioned by the Rambam. The shiur stresses recognising what is from the Torah, the Hakhamim and custom.

item.description:

item.title: 5: Daily Halacha: The Origins of Immersing in a Mikveh on Erev Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur
item.description:

item.title: 4: Daily Halacha: Sitting or Standing for Shofar
item.description:
How many shofar blasts are required, and who stands? Thirty fulfil the Torah's requirement, another thirty come in Musaf, and the total of one hundred is custom. Standing is rabbinic, learned from Sefirat HaOmer. Customs differ: Ashkenazim stand, Oriental Sephardim sit, and Spanish and Portuguese stand for the berakhah and sit for the blasts.

item.title: 6: Daily Halacha: Speaking Before Having Heard the Full Set of Shofar Blows
item.description:
When may one speak during the shofar blowing? Not at all during the first thirty blasts after the berakhah, and the Rabbi says one should not speak until the sixty have been heard, including those in the repetition of the Amidah, and try to wait until the hundred. A berakhah or other non idle speech is permitted if needed.
